sanskrit: atha haimavatīṃ rāma diśaṃ tyaktvā mahāmuniḥ pūrvāṃ diśam anuprāpya tapas tepe sudāruṇam
english: Then, O Rāma, having abandoned the Himālayan direction, the great sage reached the eastern quarter and performed exceedingly fierce austerities.

sanskrit: maunaṃ varṣasahasrasya kṛtvā vratam anuttamam cakārāpratimaṃ rāma tapaḥ paramaduṣkaram
english: Having undertaken the supreme vow of silence for a thousand years, O Rāma, he performed incomparable and supremely difficult austerities.

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu kāṣṭhabhūtaṃ mahāmunim vighnair bahubhir ādhūtaṃ krodho nāntaram āviśat
english: When the thousand years were complete, though the great sage had become like a piece of wood and was shaken by many obstacles, anger did not enter within him.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ pannagāsurarākṣasāḥ mohitās tejasā tasya tapasā mandaraśmayaḥ kaśmalopahatāḥ sarve pitāmaham athābruvan
english: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Pannagas, the Asuras, and the Rākṣasas, bewildered by his brilliant energy, their radiance dimmed by his austerities, afflicted with distress, all spoke to Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: bahubhiḥ kāraṇair deva viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ lobhitaḥ krodhitaś caiva tapasā cābhivardhate
english: "O god, the great sage Viśvāmitra, having been tempted and provoked to anger by many means, continues to grow in austerities.

sanskrit: na hy asya vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cid dṛśyate sūkṣmam apy atha na dīyate yadi tv asya manasā yad abhīpsitam vināśayati trailokyaṃ tapasā sacarācaram vyākulāś ca diśaḥ sarvā na ca kiṃ cit prakāśate
english: Not even the slightest fault is seen in him. And if what he desires in his heart is not granted, he will destroy all three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings through his austerities; all the directions are thrown into confusion and nothing shines forth.

sanskrit: sāgarāḥ kṣubhitāḥ sarve viśīryante ca parvatāḥ prakampate ca pṛthivī vāyur vāti bhṛśākulaḥ
english: All the oceans are agitated, the mountains are crumbling apart, the earth trembles, and the wind blows in extreme turmoil.

sanskrit: buddhiṃ na kurute yāvan nāśe deva mahāmuniḥ tāvat prasādyo bhagavān agnirūpo mahādyutiḥ
english: O god, so long as the great sage, blazing like fire and of great splendour, does not turn his mind toward destruction, the blessed one must be appeased.

sanskrit: kālāgninā yathā pūrvaṃ trailokyaṃ dahyate 'khilam devarājye cikīrṣeta dīyatām asya yan matam
english: Just as the fire of dissolution formerly burns all three worlds entirely — if he desires sovereignty over the gods, let what he wishes be granted to him."

sanskrit: tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve pitāmahapurogamāḥ viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānaṃ vākyaṃ madhuram abruvan
english: Then all the hosts of gods, led by Pitāmaha, spoke sweet words to the high-souled Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: brahmarṣe svāgataṃ te 'stu tapasā sma sutoṣitāḥ brāhmaṇyaṃ tapasogreṇa prāptavān asi kauśika
english: "O Brahmarṣi, be welcomed! We are thoroughly pleased by your austerities. By your fierce tapas you have attained Brahmanhood, O Kauśika.

sanskrit: dīrgham āyuś ca te brahman dadāmi samarudgaṇaḥ svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṃ te gaccha saumya yathāsukham
english: And long life to you, O Brahman, I along with the Marut hosts grant — may you attain well-being, blessings upon you; go, O gentle one, as you please."

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ mudito vyājahāra mahāmuniḥ
english: Having heard the words of Pitāmaha and all the celestials, the great sage bowed in obeisance and joyfully spoke.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyaṃ yadi me prāptaṃ dīrgham āyus tathaiva ca oṃkāro 'tha vaṣaṭkāro vedāś ca varayantu mām
english: "If Brahmanhood has been attained by me, and likewise long life — then may the Oṃkāra, the Vaṣaṭkāra, and the Vedas acknowledge me.

sanskrit: kṣatravedavidāṃ śreṣṭho brahmavedavidām api brahmaputro vasiṣṭho mām evaṃ vadatu devatāḥ yady ayaṃ paramaḥ kāmaḥ kṛto yāntu surarṣabhāḥ
english: May Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā, foremost among those who know the Vedas of the Kṣatriyas as well as the Vedas of the Brāhmaṇas, say this to me — O gods, if this supreme wish has been fulfilled, then let the foremost among gods depart."

sanskrit: tataḥ prasādito devair vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ sakhyaṃ cakāra brahmarṣir evam astv iti cābravīt
english: Then Vasiṣṭha, best among those who recite sacred texts, appeased by the gods, entered into friendship with him and spoke, saying "So be it."

sanskrit: brahmarṣitvaṃ na saṃdehaḥ sarvaṃ saṃpatsyate tava ity uktvā devatāś cāpi sarvā jagmur yathāgatam
english: "There is no doubt: the state of Brahmarṣi — all of it shall be yours." Having spoken thus, all the divinities departed as they had come.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi dharmātmā labdhvā brāhmaṇyam uttamam pūjayām āsa brahmarṣiṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam
english: And Viśvāmitra, righteous in soul, having obtained the supreme Brahmanhood, paid homage to the Brahmarṣi Vasiṣṭha, best among those who recite sacred texts.

sanskrit: kṛtakāmo mahīṃ sarvāṃ cacāra tapasi sthitaḥ evaṃ tv anena brāhmaṇyaṃ prāptaṃ rāma mahātmanā
english: His desire fulfilled, he roamed the whole earth, abiding in austerity. Thus indeed was Brahmanhood attained by this high-souled one, O Rāma.

sanskrit: eṣa rāma muniśreṣṭha eṣa vigrahavāṃs tapaḥ eṣa dharmaḥ paro nityaṃ vīryasyaiṣa parāyaṇam
english: This is the foremost of sages, O Rāma; this one is austerity in embodied form; this is the supreme eternal dharma; this is the ultimate resort of heroic power.

sanskrit: śatānandavacaḥ śrutvā rāmalakṣmaṇasaṃnidhau janakaḥ prāñjalir vākyam uvāca kuśikātmajam
english: Having heard the words of Śatānanda in the presence of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, Janaka, with palms folded, spoke to the son of Kuśika.

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yasya me munipuṃgava yajñaṃ kākutstha sahitaḥ prāptavān asi dhārmika
english: "I am blessed, I am favoured, O foremost of sages — for you, O righteous one of Kākutstha's line, have arrived together to attend my sacrifice.

sanskrit: pāvito 'haṃ tvayā brahman darśanena mahāmune guṇā bahuvidhāḥ prāptās tava saṃdarśanān mayā
english: I have been purified by you, O Brahman, by your very sight, O great sage; manifold virtues have been obtained by me through beholding you.

sanskrit: vistareṇa ca te brahman kīrtyamānaṃ mahat tapaḥ śrutaṃ mayā mahātejo rāmeṇa ca mahātmanā
english: And your great austerity narrated in full, O Brahman of mighty splendour, has been heard by me and by the high-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: sadasyaiḥ prāpya ca sadaḥ śrutās te bahavo guṇāḥ
english: And having reached this assembly along with the assembly members, your many virtues have been heard.

sanskrit: aprameyaṃ tapas tubhyam aprameyaṃ ca te balam aprameyā guṇāś caiva nityaṃ te kuśikātmaja
english: Immeasurable is your austerity, immeasurable your strength, and your virtues too are immeasurable and ever-constant, O son of Kuśika.

sanskrit: tṛptir āścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ nāsti me vibho karmakālo muniśreṣṭha lambate ravimaṇḍalam
english: I have no satiety, O lord, with these wondrous tales; but the time for ritual acts is at hand, O foremost of sages — the solar disc hangs low.

sanskrit: śvaḥ prabhāte mahātejo draṣṭum arhasi māṃ punaḥ svāgataṃ tapasāṃ śreṣṭha mām anujñātum arhasi
english: Tomorrow at dawn, O one of great splendour, please deign to see me again. You are welcome, O foremost among ascetics; now please grant me leave."

sanskrit: evam uktvā muniśreṣṭhaṃ vaideho mithilādhipaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ cakārāśu sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to the foremost of sages, the Vaideha, lord of Mithilā, together with his preceptors and kinsmen, quickly performed the circumambulation.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi dharmātmā saharāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ svaṃ vāṭam abhicakrāma pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: And Viśvāmitra, righteous in soul, along with Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, honoured by the great sages, returned to his own encampment.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtakarmā narādhipaḥ viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānam ājuhāva sarāghavam
english: Then, at the pure dawn, after completing his morning rites, the lord of men summoned the high-souled Viśvāmitra along with Rāghava.

sanskrit: tam arcayitvā dharmātmā śāstradṛṣṭtena karmaṇā rāghavau ca mahātmānau tadā vākyam uvāca ha
english: Having worshipped him, the righteous-souled king, with rites prescribed by the scriptures, then spoke these words to both the high-souled Rāghavas.

sanskrit: bhagavan svāgataṃ te 'stu kiṃ karomi tavānagha bhavān ājñāpayatu mām ājñāpyo bhavatā hy aham
english: "O blessed one, be welcome. What shall I do for you, O sinless one? You must command me; I am indeed one who is to be commanded by you."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā janakena mahātmanā pratyuvāca munir vīraṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the high-souled Janaka, that righteous-souled sage, eloquent in speech, replied to the hero with these words.

sanskrit: putrau daśarathasyemau kṣatriyau lokaviśrutau draṣṭukāmau dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ yad etat tvayi tiṣṭhati
english: "These two sons of Daśaratha, Kṣatriyas famed throughout the world, are desirous of seeing the supreme bow that stands in your keeping.

sanskrit: etad darśaya bhadraṃ te kṛtakāmau nṛpātmajau darśanād asya dhanuṣo yatheṣṭaṃ pratiyāsyataḥ
english: Show it to them — good fortune to you! Once the wishes of these two princes are fulfilled by sight of this bow, they shall depart as they desire."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu janakaḥ pratyuvāca mahāmunim śrūyatām asya dhanuṣo yad artham iha tiṣṭhati
english: Thus addressed, Janaka replied to the great sage: "Hear the purpose for which this bow stands here.

sanskrit: devarāta iti khyāto nimeḥ ṣaṣṭho mahīpatiḥ nyāso 'yaṃ tasya bhagavan haste datto mahātmanā
english: There was a renowned king called Devarāta, the sixth descendant of Nimi — this bow, O blessed one, was a trust deposited by that high-souled one into his keeping.

sanskrit: dakṣayajñavadhe pūrvaṃ dhanur āyamya vīryavān rudras tu tridaśān roṣāt salīlam idam abravīt
english: Formerly, at the destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice, the mighty Rudra, having strung this bow, sportively and in anger spoke thus to the thirty gods.

sanskrit: yasmād bhāgārthino bhāgān nākalpayata me surāḥ varāṅgāni mahārhāṇi dhanuṣā śātayāmi vaḥ
english: "Since the gods, though desiring their shares, did not apportion a share to me, I shall cut off your most excellent and precious limbs with this bow."

sanskrit: tato vimanasaḥ sarve devā vai munipuṃgava prasādayanti deveśaṃ teṣāṃ prīto 'bhavad bhavaḥ
english: Then all the gods, O foremost of sages, being downcast, propitiated the Lord of Gods; and Bhava became pleased with them.

sanskrit: prītiyuktaḥ sa sarveṣāṃ dadau teṣāṃ mahātmanām
english: Filled with satisfaction, he gave it to all those high-souled ones.

sanskrit: tad etad devadevasya dhanūratnaṃ mahātmanaḥ nyāsabhūtaṃ tadā nyastam asmākaṃ pūrvake vibho
english: This very jewel of a bow belonging to the great-souled God of gods was then deposited as a trust in the keeping of our ancestors, O lord.

sanskrit: atha me kṛṣataḥ kṣetraṃ lāṅgalād utthitā mama kṣetraṃ śodhayatā labdhvā nāmnā sīteti viśrutā
english: Then, as I was ploughing the field, one was born who rose from the furrow — obtained by me while purifying the field, she became known by the name Sītā.

sanskrit: bhūtalād utthitā sā tu vyavardhata mamātmajā vīryaśulketi me kanyā sthāpiteyam ayonijā
english: She who arose from the surface of the earth grew up as my daughter; this girl not born of a womb was established by me as one whose bride-price is valour.

sanskrit: bhūtalād utthitāṃ tāṃ tu vardhamānāṃ mamātmajām varayām āsur āgamya rājāno munipuṃgava
english: And as she grew, this daughter of mine who rose from the earth — kings came, O foremost of sages, to sue for her hand.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ varayatāṃ kanyāṃ sarveṣāṃ pṛthivīkṣitām vīryaśulketi bhagavan na dadāmi sutām aham
english: To all those rulers of the earth who sought my daughter's hand, I answered: O blessed one, I do not give my daughter — her bride-price is valour.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve nṛpatayaḥ sametya munipuṃgava mithilām abhyupāgamya vīryaṃ jijñāsavas tadā
english: Then all the kings, O foremost of sages, assembled and came to Mithilā at that time, wishing to test their valour.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ vīryaṃ dhanur upāhṛtam na śekur grahaṇe tasya dhanuṣas tolane 'pi vā
english: For them who wished to prove their valour, the bow was brought out; but they were unable even to lift or to take hold of that bow.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vīryavatāṃ vīryam alpaṃ jñātvā mahāmune pratyākhyātā nṛpatayo tan nibodha tapodhana
english: Knowing the valour of those valiant ones to be insufficient, O great sage, the kings were rejected — hear that, O wealth of austerity.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramakopena rājāno munipuṃgava arundhan mithilāṃ sarve vīryasaṃdeham āgatāḥ
english: Then, O foremost of sages, in extreme anger and with their valour in doubt, all the kings besieged Mithilā.

sanskrit: ātmānam avadhūtaṃ te vijñāya munipuṃgava roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭāḥ pīḍayan mithilāṃ purīm
english: Perceiving themselves to have been spurned, O foremost of sages, those kings, seized by great rage, afflicted the city of Mithilā.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe kṣayaṃ yātāni sarvaśaḥ sādhanāni munireṣṭha tato 'haṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: Then, when a full year had passed, all resources were utterly exhausted, O most revered of sages, and I was deeply distressed.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇān sarvāṃs tapasāhaṃ prasādayam daduś ca paramaprītāś caturaṅgabalaṃ surāḥ
english: Then I propitiated all the hosts of gods through austerity, and the gods, most graciously pleased, gave me a fourfold army.

sanskrit: tato bhagnā nṛpatayo hanyamānā diśo yayuḥ avīryā vīryasaṃdigdhā sāmātyāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ
english: Then the kings, broken and slain, fled in all directions — those evildoers devoid of valour, their boasted valour now in doubt, along with their ministers.

sanskrit: tad etan muniśārdūla dhanuḥ paramabhāsvaram rāmalakṣmaṇayoś cāpi darśayiṣyāmi suvrata
english: That supremely radiant bow, O tiger among sages, I shall show also to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, O one of excellent vows.

sanskrit: yady asya dhanuṣo rāmaḥ kuryād āropaṇaṃ mune sutām ayonijāṃ sītāṃ dadyāṃ dāśarather aham
english: If Rāma should string this bow, O sage, I would give my daughter Sītā, not born of a womb, to the son of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ dhanur darśaya rāmāya iti hovāca pārthivam
english: Having heard the words of Janaka, the great sage Viśvāmitra said to the king: "Show the bow to Rāma."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā janakaḥ sacivān vyādideśa ha dhanur ānīyatāṃ divyaṃ gandhamālyavibhūṣitam
english: Then King Janaka commanded his ministers: "Let the divine bow, adorned with garlands of fragrant flowers, be brought."

sanskrit: janakena samādiṣṭhāḥ sacivāḥ prāviśan purīm tad dhanuḥ purataḥ kṛtvā nirjagmuḥ pārthivājñayā
english: Commanded by Janaka, the ministers entered the city; placing that bow at their head, they emerged by the king's command.

sanskrit: nṛpāṃ śatāni pañcāśad vyāyatānāṃ mahātmanām mañjūṣām aṣṭacakrāṃ tāṃ samūhus te kathaṃ cana
english: Five hundred men, tall and strong of great spirit, with great difficulty drew along that chest mounted on eight wheels.

sanskrit: tām ādāya tu mañjūṣām āyatīṃ yatra tad dhanuḥ suropamaṃ te janakam ūcur nṛpatimantriṇaḥ
english: Taking that great chest in which the bow lay, divine in its appearance, the royal ministers addressed Janaka.

sanskrit: idaṃ dhanurvaraṃ rājan pūjitaṃ sarvarājabhiḥ mithilādhipa rājendra darśanīyaṃ yadīcchasi
english: "This supreme bow, O king, honoured by all kings — O lord of Mithilā, O best of kings, it may now be displayed if you so desire."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ nṛpo vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānaṃ tau cobhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: The king, having heard their words, with palms folded, spoke to the high-souled Viśvāmitra and to those two — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: idaṃ dhanurvaraṃ brahmañ janakair abhipūjitam rājabhiś ca mahāvīryair aśakyaṃ pūrituṃ tadā
english: "This supreme bow, O Brahman, has been worshipped by the Janakas and by kings of great valour; even then it could not be strung.

sanskrit: naitat suragaṇāḥ sarve nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ gandharvayakṣapravarāḥ sakiṃnaramahoragāḥ
english: Not all the hosts of gods, nor Asuras, nor Rākṣasas, nor the foremost Gandharvas and Yakṣas, nor Kiṃnaras and great serpents —

sanskrit: kva gatir mānuṣāṇāṃ ca dhanuṣo 'sya prapūraṇe āropaṇe samāyoge vepane tolane 'pi vā
english: — what then is the recourse of human beings in stringing, drawing, fastening the bowstring to, bending, or even merely lifting this bow?

sanskrit: tad etad dhanuṣāṃ śreṣṭham ānītaṃ munipuṃgava darśayaitan mahābhāga anayo rājaputrayoḥ
english: This best of bows has been brought, O foremost of sages; O most blessed one, show it to these two princes."

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu dharmātmā śrutvā janakabhāṣitam vatsa rāma dhanuḥ paśya iti rāghavam abravīt
english: And Viśvāmitra, righteous in soul, having heard what Janaka said, spoke to the Rāghava: "Child Rāma, behold the bow."

sanskrit: maharṣer vacanād rāmo yatra tiṣṭhati tad dhanuḥ mañjūṣāṃ tām apāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā dhanur athābravīt
english: At the great sage's word, Rāma went to where the bow stood, and having opened that chest and looked at the bow, he then spoke.

sanskrit: idaṃ dhanurvaraṃ brahman saṃspṛśāmīha pāṇinā yatnavāṃś ca bhaviṣyāmi tolane pūraṇe 'pi vā
english: "O Brahman, I shall touch this supreme bow with my hand, and I shall make effort in lifting and stringing it as well."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva taṃ rājā muniś ca samabhāṣata līlayā sa dhanur madhye jagrāha vacanān muneḥ
english: "Certainly!" — thus the king and the sage both replied to him. At the sage's word, he took hold of the bow in the middle, as if in play.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ nṛṣahasrāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ raghunandanaḥ āropayat sa dharmātmā salīlam iva tad dhanuḥ
english: Before the gaze of many thousands of men, the delight of the Raghu clan, righteous in soul, strung that bow as if in sport.

sanskrit: āropayitvā maurvīṃ ca pūrayām āsa vīryavān tad babhañja dhanur madhye naraśreṣṭho mahāyaśāḥ
english: And having strung the bowstring, the valiant one drew it to the full; then the foremost of men, of great glory, broke the bow in the middle.

sanskrit: tasya śabdo mahān āsīn nirghātasamanisvanaḥ bhūmikampaś ca sumahān parvatasyeva dīryataḥ
english: Its sound was tremendous, like the roar of a thunderclap; and there was a very great trembling of the earth, as if a mountain were splitting asunder.

sanskrit: nipetuś ca narāḥ sarve tena śabdena mohitāḥ varjayitvā munivaraṃ rājānaṃ tau ca rāghavau
english: And all the people fell to the ground, bewildered by that sound — all except the foremost sage, the king, and those two Rāghavas.

sanskrit: pratyāśvaste jane tasmin rājā vigatasādhvasaḥ uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ vākyajño munipuṃgavam
english: When the people had recovered, the king, his fear gone, with palms folded and skilled in speech, spoke these words to the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: bhagavan dṛṣṭavīryo me rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ atyadbhutam acintyaṃ ca atarkitam idaṃ mayā
english: "O blessed one, the valour of Rāma, son of Daśaratha, has been seen by me; this is utterly wondrous and inconceivable, unimagined by me.

sanskrit: janakānāṃ kule kīrtim āhariṣyati me sutā sītā bhartāram āsādya rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
english: My daughter Sītā will bring glory to the lineage of the Janakas, having obtained as husband Rāma, son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: mama satyā pratijñā ca vīryaśulketi kauśika sītā prāṇair bahumatā deyā rāmāya me sutā
english: And my pledge stands true — valour is the bride-price, O Kauśika; Sītā, held by me dearer than life itself, must be given to Rāma.

sanskrit: bhavato 'numate brahmañ śīghraṃ gacchantu mantriṇaḥ mama kauśika bhadraṃ te ayodhyāṃ tvaritā rathaiḥ
english: With your permission, O Brahman, let my ministers go quickly — O Kauśika, blessings upon you — to Ayodhyā swiftly by chariots.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ praśritair vākyair ānayantu puraṃ mama pradānaṃ vīryaśulkāyāḥ kathayantu ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Let them bring the king here to my city with respectful words, and let them recount everything about the gift of one whose bride-price was valour.

sanskrit: muniguptau ca kākutsthau kathayantu nṛpāya vai prīyamāṇaṃ tu rājānam ānayantu suśīghragāḥ
english: Let them also tell the king of the two Kākutsthas under the sage's protection, and let those swift messengers bring the delighted king here.

sanskrit: kauśikaś ca tathety āha rājā cābhāṣya mantriṇaḥ ayodhyāṃ preṣayām āsa dharmātmā kṛtaśāsanāt
english: Kauśika said "So be it"; and the king, righteous in soul, addressing his ministers, dispatched them to Ayodhyā as commanded.
